3.2.2 Species and Ecosystems
3.2.2.1 Flora
The wide fluctuation of the upper reservoir would probably practude the establishment of any emergent plant species in the fluctuation zone. Fluctuation of the lower reservoir, Lake Jocassee, is of a much smaller magnitude. Thus, emergent species would not be significantly affected by fluctuations in the lower reservoir caused by Bad Creek.
3.2.2.2 Wildlife
Most terrestrial wildlife would be permanently excluded from approximately 370 acres in the immediate reservoir area as a direct result of the mode of project operation or as a consequence of peripheral fencing of the upper reservoir. Approximately 90 acres of additional lands planned for use as tunnel portals and other facilities would be permanently altered and would generally be unavailable to wildlife.
A limited area of habitat suitable for vertebrates and small vertebrate fauna would be available in the form of border strips of vegetation near the edge of the reservoir within the project boundary. Other vegetation would develop as a result of Applicant's planned rehabilitation efforts. Any organisms that survive the construction impacts described in Subsection 3.1.2 and other fauna gaining access to the area would be expected in time to fully utilize available food resources and suitable habitats within the proposed project area. Avian species would have unrestricted access. Operational impacts on endangered species or on those species listed on the undetermined categories would vary with the species. Greatest impacts would be on resident forms having low mobility and restricted to specific environmental requirements (see Subsection 2.2.3). Probably the most susceptible form would be the green salamander. Cleared areas of transmission line rights-of-way described in Subsection 3.1.2 would be maintained in perpetual early plant successional stages which would benefit deer and other wildlife species dependent on open areas for food and nesting cover. Selective cutting of trees that interfere with line clearance requirements would have a minor impact on local wildlife forms.
